_comment: CR-390: Menu Management module manifest — 36-screen journey approved by owner 2026-09-27 (expanded from 10). Read-only capture: no Save/Delete/Confirm is ever pressed.

overview.summary: Menu Management is where the restaurant builds and maintains everything a guest can order: categories, items, prices, taxes, variations (sizes / spice levels), add-ons, images, channel availability (Dine-In, Delivery, Takeaway, Live Web) and the separate Aggregator menu that is pushed to Swiggy and Zomato. It offers three editing speeds — Quick Edit on the card, a Full Edit form, and a spreadsheet-style Bulk Editor with Excel import/export — plus drag-and-drop ordering that controls how the menu appears on the POS order screen.
overview.who_uses: Owner and Manager roles (permission 'food'). Typically used at menu launch, seasonal price revisions, daily out-of-stock marking, and when onboarding a new delivery aggregator.
key_capabilities: Multiple menus — Normal, Party, Premium, Aggregator — switched from one dropdown; a station picks its Active Menu in Local Settings
Categories — create, rename, delete, assign a kitchen station / printer, drag to reorder
Items — card view with search and Active / Inactive / Veg / Non-Veg / Egg / Jain filters; drag to reorder inside a category
Quick Edit — the 12 most-changed fields inline on the card (price, tax, category, food type, flags)
Full Edit / Add Item — image upload, description, pricing & tax, discounts, classification, availability window, variations, add-ons, operations timings & charges, status flags
Add-ons master — one list of add-ons (price, weight, veg flag, inventory / recipe link) reused across items
Bulk Editor — spreadsheet grid, column picker by tier, dirty-cell tracking, Validate Tax, multi-select delete with reason, Excel download (all / template) and upload
Aggregator menu — Swiggy / Zomato sync flags, Swiggy-specific image, per-item stock ON / OFF with automatic turn-on time, Addon Stock and Variation Stock tabs

states.title: Opening Menu Management from the sidebar
states.description: Menu Management lives in the left navigation sidebar of the POS. With the sidebar expanded, the 'Menu Management' entry (fork-and-knife icon) is visible in the main list. Clicking it opens the module as a full page at /menu.
controls: Sidebar expand / collapse arrow — widens the sidebar to show labels next to icons
Menu Management entry — opens the module; highlighted in orange when active
Restaurant profile block (bottom) — shows the logged-in restaurant and role
states.narration: From anywhere in MyGenie, open the sidebar and tap Menu Management. This is the home of every category, item, price and add-on your guests can order.

states.title: Menu Management landing — Card View
states.description: The default view. The left column (30%) lists categories with an item count badge; the right column (70%) shows item cards for the selected category ('All' by default). The header holds the menu-type dropdown and the three mode buttons: Add-ons, Bulk Edit and Close.
controls: Menu type dropdown — switches between Normal, Party, Premium and Aggregator menus; everything below reloads
Add-ons button — opens the add-ons master panel
Bulk Edit button — swaps the card view for the spreadsheet Bulk Editor (label becomes 'Card View' to switch back)
Close (X) — returns to the previous page
Category column — 'All' plus every category with its item count; click one to filter the cards
Item column — search box, Filters toggle and green '+ Add' button above the item cards
Loading… indicator — appears next to the title while items are being fetched
states.narration: This is the Card View. Categories on the left, items on the right. The dropdown at the top decides which menu you are editing.

states.title: Switching menus — Premium menu selected
states.description: Each restaurant can run several menus. Selecting 'Premium' reloads categories, counts and cards for that menu only. Party and Premium menus are priced independently from Normal; Aggregator is the Swiggy / Zomato catalogue.
controls: Menu type dropdown — lists every menu configured for the restaurant (Normal / Party / Premium / Aggregator)
Item counts — recalculated for the chosen menu
Item cards — show the Premium prices and availability chips
states.narration: Need a separate party or premium price list? Switch menus here. Every card and count you see now belongs to the Premium menu only.

states.title: Category column — search, counts and station
states.description: Categories are the top-level grouping guests see on the order screen. Each row shows the drag grip (⋮⋮), the category name, the kitchen station / printer it routes to (small grey text) and a count badge of items in it. The list has its own search box and an '+ Add Category' button at the bottom.
controls: Search categories — filters the list as you type
All — clears the category filter and shows every item
Category row — click to show only that category's items (row turns orange with a left bar)
Drag grip ⋮⋮ (left of each row) — press-and-hold to reorder categories; the order is what the POS shows
Station label — the printer / KDS station this category's KOTs go to
Count badge — number of items in the category for the current menu
+ Add Category — opens the inline create form
states.narration: Categories drive both the guest-facing order screen and kitchen routing. The grey label under each name is the station its KOTs print to.

states.title: Category row hover — rename and delete
states.description: Hovering a category row reveals its two actions on the right: a pencil (rename / change station) and a red trash (delete). Actions are hidden until hover to keep the list clean.
controls: Pencil — turns the row into an inline edit form (name + station dropdown)
Trash — asks 'Delete?' inline with Yes / No before removing the category
Drag grip — becomes fully visible on hover
states.narration: Hover any category to reveal rename and delete. Nothing is deleted without a confirmation.

states.title: Rename a category / change its station
states.description: The inline edit form replaces the row: a text box for the name and a station dropdown (KDS or any configured printer station). The printer icon confirms which physical printer the station maps to. Save commits, Cancel or Escape discards.
controls: Name input — Enter saves, Escape cancels
Station dropdown — KDS / kitchen / bar etc.; decides where KOTs for this category print
Printer hint — shows the printer bound to the selected station, or a warning if none
Save — writes the change and refreshes the list
Cancel — discards
states.narration: Renaming or re-routing a category to a different kitchen printer is a two-second inline edit.

states.title: Delete a category — inline confirmation
states.description: Clicking the trash icon opens a small red confirmation strip under the row: 'Delete?' with No / Yes. Only Yes removes the category. (Not pressed in this guide.)
controls: Yes — deletes the category (items must be moved first if any remain)
No — closes the strip
states.narration: Deleting asks for a confirmation right in place, so a stray click never removes a category.

states.title: Add Category form
states.description: The '+ Add Category' button opens an inline form at the bottom of the column: category name, station dropdown (defaults to KDS) and the printer hint. Add saves and the new category appears immediately with a 0 count.
controls: Category name — required
Station dropdown — choose the kitchen station for KOT routing
Printer hint — which printer that station uses
Add — creates the category
Cancel — closes the form
states.narration: Adding a category is name plus station. The station matters: it decides which kitchen printer gets the ticket.

states.title: Drag-and-drop category ordering
states.description: Press-and-hold the ⋮⋮ grip and move the row. The lifted row turns light orange and the others shift to make room. Releasing saves the new order, which is the order guests and staff see on the order screen. There is no separate 'reorder' button — drag is always on.
controls: Drag grip ⋮⋮ — the only handle; press, move, release
Lifted row (orange tint) — the category being moved
Gap — where it will land on release
states.narration: To reorder categories just grab the grip and drag. The lifted row glows orange; drop it where you want it and the POS follows that order.

states.title: Item cards — what each card tells you
states.description: With a category selected, each item is a card. Left to right: drag grip, food-type square (green veg / red non-veg / yellow egg / purple jain), item name with an 'Inactive' tag when switched off, the category · food-type line, and a row of chips: Dine-In / Delivery / Takeaway availability (green when on), plus Inventory, Packaged, Out of Stock, Hidden and Tax Incl. badges when applicable. The price sits on the right.
controls: Food-type square — colour-codes veg / non-veg / egg / jain
Channel chips — Dine-In, Delivery, Takeaway; green = item is sold on that channel
Inventory badge — item consumes stock from Inventory
Packaged badge — pre-packaged product (no kitchen prep)
Out of Stock badge — temporarily unavailable
Hidden badge — hidden from the POS order screen
Tax Incl. badge — price already includes tax
Price — base price in restaurant currency
states.narration: Every card is a one-line status report: what kind of food it is, where it is sold, whether it is in stock, and what it costs.

states.title: Search and filter items
states.description: The search box matches item names live. The Filters button reveals two chip rows: Status (All / Active / Inactive) and Food type (All / Veg / Non-Veg / Egg / Jain). Filters combine with the selected category.
controls: Search products — live text filter on item name
Filters toggle — shows / hides the chip rows (orange when open)
Status chips — All, Active, Inactive
Food type chips — All, Veg, Non-Veg, Egg, Jain (each in its colour)
+ Add — opens the blank Add Item form
states.narration: Looking for every inactive non-veg item? Open Filters, tap Inactive and Non-Veg, and the list narrows instantly.

states.title: Item card hover — the four action buttons
states.description: Hovering a card reveals four icon buttons at the right edge, next to the price: Power (Activate / Deactivate), Lightning (Quick Edit), Pencil (Full Edit) and Trash (Delete). The drag grip on the left also becomes fully visible.
controls: Power (green) — toggles the item Active / Inactive instantly, no form
Lightning (amber) — opens Quick Edit inline on the card
Pencil (grey) — opens the Full Edit form for every field
Trash (red) — opens the delete-with-reason confirmation
Drag grip ⋮⋮ — press-and-hold to reorder the item within its category
states.narration: Hover a card and four buttons appear: switch it on or off, quick edit, full edit, or delete. The grip on the left lets you drag it.

states.title: Drag-and-drop item ordering
states.description: Same gesture as categories: hold the ⋮⋮ grip on a card and move it. The card turns orange while lifted; releasing writes the new sort order for that category so the POS shows items in this sequence.
controls: Drag grip ⋮⋮ — press-and-hold, move, release
Lifted card (orange border) — item being moved
Gap — landing position
states.narration: Put your best-sellers at the top: hold the grip, drag the card, release. The POS order screen follows this order.

states.title: Inactive item — how it looks
states.description: An item switched off with the Power button stays in the list but is greyed out, gets an 'Inactive' tag next to its name and its price is dimmed. It will not appear on the POS order screen until switched back on. Filtering by Status = Inactive lists them all.
controls: Inactive tag — grey pill next to the name
Dimmed card — 70% opacity, grey background
Power button — re-activates on click
states.narration: Switched-off items stay visible to managers but vanish from the order screen. One tap on the power icon brings them back.

states.title: Quick Edit — inline on the card
states.description: Quick Edit expands the card into a compact form with the fields that change most often: Name, Sold By (unit), Category (with a '+' to create one), Price, Food Type, Complementary, Tax Type / Tax %, Tax Calc (Inclusive / Exclusive), Inventory and Packaged. Save writes immediately; Cancel collapses the card unchanged.
controls: Name — item name
Sold By (Unit) — Piece / Kg / Ltr etc.
Category dropdown + '+' — move the item or create a new category on the spot
Price — base price
Food Type — Veg / Non-Veg / Egg / Jain
Complementary — Yes / No (free item)
Tax Type — GST / VAT / None, with Tax %
Tax Calc — Inclusive or Exclusive of the price
Inventory / Packaged — Yes / No flags
Save (green) — commits; Cancel — discards
states.narration: For a price or tax change you do not need the full form. Quick Edit puts the twelve everyday fields right on the card.

states.title: Delete an item — reason required
states.description: The trash button opens a red confirmation strip inside the card: 'Delete "item"?' with a mandatory reason dropdown (reasons come from the restaurant's configured list). The Delete button stays disabled until a reason is chosen. (Not pressed in this guide.)
controls: Reason dropdown — mandatory; pre-configured delete reasons
Delete (red) — enabled only after a reason is selected
Cancel — closes the strip
states.narration: Deleting an item always records why. Pick a reason, then confirm — or cancel.

states.title: Full Edit — name, unit, description and Item Image
states.description: The Full Edit form (pencil on a card, or '+ Add' for a new item) replaces the item column. The top block holds Name, Sold By (Unit), Description and the Item Image uploader: a thumbnail preview with an X to remove and an Upload / Change button that accepts any image file. Below it the form is organised into collapsible sections.
controls: Back arrow — returns to the card list without saving
Name — required
Sold By (Unit) — Piece / Kg / Ltr / Plate etc.
Description — shown to guests on Live Web and aggregators
Item Image: Upload / Change — picks an image file; preview appears at once
Item Image: X — removes the current image
Section headers — click to expand / collapse each group of fields
Save (bottom) — writes all sections in one call
states.narration: The Full Edit form covers everything. Start at the top: name, unit, description and the photo guests will see online.

states.title: Pricing & Tax and Classification sections
states.description: Pricing & Tax: Category (required), Price, Tax Type (GST / VAT / None) with Tax %, and an Allow Discount toggle that reveals Discount amount + Type (flat / percent). Classification: Item Code, Food Type selector, Allergens text and Kcal.
controls: Category — required dropdown
Price — base selling price
Tax Type + Tax % — GST / VAT / None and the rate
Allow Discount — toggle; when on, Discount and Type (Flat / Percent) appear
Item Code — internal SKU / code
Food Type — Veg / Non-Veg / Egg / Jain
Allergens — free text, e.g. Milk, Nuts
Kcal — calorie value shown to guests
states.narration: Pricing and tax live together: price, GST or VAT and the rate. Allow Discount lets this item accept a flat or percentage discount.

states.title: Availability & Channels — where and when it sells
states.description: Four channel toggles decide where the item is orderable: Dine-In, Delivery, Takeaway and Live Web (online ordering). Available From / Until define a daily time window (e.g. breakfast items 07:00–11:00); outside it the item is hidden on the order screen.
controls: Dine-In — sell on table orders
Delivery — sell on delivery orders
Takeaway — sell on parcel / pickup orders
Live Web (Online Ordering) — publish on the restaurant's web ordering page
Available From / Available Until — daily time window (24h)
states.narration: Decide where and when the item is sold: any mix of Dine-In, Delivery, Takeaway and web, and an optional daily time window.

states.title: Food Variations — sizes, portions, spice levels
states.description: A variation is a named group of options a guest must (or may) choose from — Size: Regular / Large, Spice: Mild / Hot. Each group has a name, Single or Multi select, a Required checkbox, Min / Max picks for multi, and a list of options each with its own extra price. Groups and options can be added or deleted freely.
controls: Variation name — e.g. Size, Spice Level
Single / Multi — one choice or several
Required — guest must choose before adding to order
Min / Max (multi only) — bounds on number of picks
Option rows — label + extra price; trash removes an option
+ Add option — new option row
+ Add New Variation — new group
Group trash — removes the whole variation
states.narration: Variations turn one item into many: sizes, portions or spice levels, each with its own price. Mark a group Required and the cashier must pick before adding.

states.title: Food Addons — attach existing or create new
states.description: Add-ons are optional extras (extra cheese, fries) drawn from the restaurant's Add-ons master. The section lists every add-on with a checkbox and price; ticked ones are offered with this item. Below the list a mini-form creates a brand-new add-on (name, Veg / Non-Veg, price) without leaving the item.
controls: Add-on checkboxes — tick to attach; badge shows how many are selected
New add-on name — text
Veg / Non-Veg — dropdown
Price — extra charge
Add — creates the add-on in the master and refreshes the list
states.narration: Tick the add-ons this item can carry. Need a new one? Create it right here — it lands in the master list for every other item too.

states.title: Operations and Status & Flags sections
states.description: Operations holds kitchen timing and per-item charges: Prep Time and Serve Time in minutes (feed the KDS and prep-time reports), Pack Charges, Takeaway Charge and Delivery Charge. Status & Flags has five toggles: Complementary, Inventory Item, Packaged Item, Out of Stock and Hidden from POS.
controls: Prep Time (min) — expected kitchen time; drives KDS colour and reports
Serve Time (min) — expected time to table
Pack Charges / Takeaway Charge / Delivery Charge — per-item add-on charges by channel
Complementary — item is offered free
Inventory Item — consumes stock from the Inventory module
Packaged Item — pre-packaged, no kitchen ticket
Out of Stock — temporarily unavailable; shows a red badge
Hidden from POS — keep in the menu but hide from order taking
Save Item — commits every section
states.narration: Operations sets prep and serve times plus packing and delivery charges. Status & Flags is where you mark an item out of stock or hide it from the POS.

states.title: Add Item — blank form
states.description: The green '+ Add' button above the cards opens the same form empty. Required fields are Name, Category and Price; everything else has sensible defaults (GST, Exclusive tax, all channels on). Saving creates the item in the currently selected menu.
controls: + Add (card view) — opens this blank form
Required: Name, Category, Price
Defaults — Food Type Veg, Tax Type GST, all channels on, no variations / add-ons
Save Item — creates the item in the active menu type
states.narration: Adding a new dish starts from the plus button. Fill name, category and price — the rest is optional — and save.

states.title: Add-ons panel — the shared add-on list
states.description: The Add-ons button in the header opens the master list. Every add-on has a name, price, weight in grams, Veg / Non-Veg flag, an Inventory checkbox (deduct stock) and, when a recipe is attached, recipe-linked costing. Add-ons defined here are what items pick from in their Food Addons section.
controls: Search add-ons — live filter
+ Add add-on — inline row: Name, Price, Weight g, Veg / Non-Veg
Pencil — edit a row inline
Inventory checkbox — deduct from stock when sold (needs a recipe first)
Trash — delete the add-on
Close — back to Card View
states.narration: Add-ons are managed once, here, and reused across every item. Price, weight, veg flag and whether it draws from inventory.

states.title: Add-ons panel — creating a new add-on
states.description: Clicking '+ Add' inserts an editable row at the top: Name, Price, Weight (g) and Veg / Non-Veg. Save creates it; Cancel discards. The new add-on is instantly available to every item.
controls: Name — required
Price — extra charge when chosen
Weight g — for portion / inventory maths
Veg / Non-Veg — dropdown
Save / Cancel
states.narration: A new add-on is a single row: name, price, weight, veg flag, save.

states.title: Bulk Editor — spreadsheet view of the whole menu
states.description: Bulk Edit turns the menu into an editable grid: one row per item, one column per field. Cells edit in place; changed cells turn orange and the Save button shows a count. The toolbar offers Search, Columns, Download Excel, Upload Excel, + Add Row, Validate Tax and Save Changes.
controls: Search items — filters rows
Columns — picker to show / hide columns by tier
Download Excel ▾ — All items, or a blank Template
Upload Excel — import an .xlsx to add / update items
+ Add Row — new blank item row
Validate Tax — checks tax type / % consistency across rows
Save Changes (n) — writes every dirty row in one go
Select-all checkbox — for multi-select delete
Img / Name / Category / Price / Add-ons / Variations / Status / Type / Tax columns — tier-1 defaults
Card View — back to cards
states.narration: When you have a hundred prices to change, use the Bulk Editor. Edit cells like a spreadsheet, then save everything at once.

states.title: Column picker — choose which fields to edit
states.description: Columns are grouped in tiers: Tier 1 essentials (name, category, price, tax, status), Tier 2 channels & flags, Tier 3 operations & charges, Tier 4 nutrition. Tick a column to add it to the grid; Name and Image are always shown.
controls: Tier groups — expand to see the columns in each
Checkbox per column — show / hide
Always visible — Img and Name cannot be hidden
states.narration: Only see what you are editing. The column picker shows fields by tier — from essentials to nutrition.

states.title: Download Excel — all items or blank template
states.description: The Download Excel menu exports the grid to .xlsx. 'Export all' writes every item with its current values (ideal for offline price revisions); 'Template' writes only the headers for adding brand-new items. Both files re-import through Upload Excel.
controls: Export all items — full menu as Excel
Export template — headers only, for new items
Upload Excel — imports .xlsx / .xls; a confirmation dialog summarises adds vs updates before anything is written
states.narration: Take the menu to Excel, change prices offline, upload it back. The template gives you the exact columns for new items.

states.title: Filter strip and inline cell editing
states.description: The filter strip narrows rows by category and by quick chips (e.g. Active, Inactive, Veg). Any cell can be edited directly: text and numbers by typing, dropdowns by selecting, Yes / No flags by clicking. A changed cell is tinted orange until saved; Reset All undoes everything.
controls: Category select — show one category's rows
Quick chips — status / food-type filters
Clear — removes all filters
Cell edit — click a cell and type or pick
Orange cell — unsaved change
Reset All / Save (footer) — discard or commit all dirty rows
states.narration: Filter down to the rows you need, edit cells in place — orange means unsaved — and commit with Save.

states.title: Add-ons and Variations expand inside a row
states.description: The Add-ons and Variations columns show a count chip. Clicking the chip expands a panel under the row: for add-ons, checkboxes for every master add-on; for variations, the groups and options with prices. This lets you attach add-ons or review variations for many items without opening each Full Edit form.
controls: Add-ons chip — click to expand the add-on checklist
Variations chip — click to expand variation groups (disabled when 0)
Checkbox per add-on — attach / detach; marks the row dirty
Collapse — click the chip again
states.narration: Attach add-ons in bulk: click the chip on any row, tick the add-ons, move to the next row.

states.title: Multi-select rows — bulk delete banner
states.description: Ticking row checkboxes shows an orange banner with the selected count and a 'Delete selected' button. Deleting opens a dialog that requires a reason (same list as single delete). Clear deselects everything. (Dialog is cancelled in this guide.)
controls: Row checkbox — select an item
Select-all checkbox (header) — select every visible row
Banner count — how many are selected
Delete selected — opens the reason dialog
Clear — deselect all
states.narration: Retiring a whole section of the menu? Tick the rows, hit Delete selected, give a reason.

states.title: Bulk delete — reason dialog
states.description: The confirmation dialog names how many items will be deleted and asks for a reason from the configured list. Confirm is disabled until a reason is chosen; Cancel closes without changes.
controls: Reason for deletion — dropdown, mandatory
Confirm delete — enabled after a reason is picked
Cancel — closes the dialog
states.narration: Bulk delete still needs a reason — the same audit trail as deleting one item.

states.title: Aggregator menu — Card View
states.description: Selecting 'Aggregator' in the menu dropdown shows the catalogue that syncs to Swiggy and Zomato. Cards swap the Dine-In / Delivery / Takeaway chips for Swiggy and Zomato chips (green = listed) and gain a stock pill on the right ('Live' or 'Off · back at HH:MM'). An 'Aggregator Stock' button appears in the header. When the restaurant runs sub-brands, a Brand selector (All / Main Branch / brand) also appears.
controls: Menu type = Aggregator — switches to the aggregator catalogue
Swiggy / Zomato chips — whether the item is listed on each platform
Stock pill — click to take the item offline / online on the aggregators
Offline · Back at … badge — item is off with an automatic turn-on time
Aggregator Stock button — opens Addon Stock / Variation Stock tabs
Brand selector — filter by sub-brand (only when sub-brands exist)
states.narration: The Aggregator menu is what Swiggy and Zomato customers see. Each card shows its platform listing and a live stock pill.

states.title: Item stock toggle — take offline until a time
states.description: Clicking the stock pill opens a small popover. Turning an item OFF asks for a turn-on time (or 'until I switch it on'); the item is instantly marked out-of-stock on Swiggy and Zomato and shows an 'Offline · Back at' badge. Turning ON re-lists it at once.
controls: Turn-on time options — e.g. 30 min, 1 h, tomorrow, manual
Confirm — pushes the stock change to the aggregators
Cancel — closes without change
Enable (when offline) — brings the item back live
states.narration: Ran out of a dish mid-shift? Tap the pill, pick when it will be back, confirm — Swiggy and Zomato update immediately.

states.title: Quick Edit on an aggregator item — Swiggy / Zomato / Brand
states.description: Quick Edit in Aggregator mode adds a top row: Swiggy (Yes / No), Zomato (Yes / No) and Brand (Main or a sub-brand), plus the Swiggy Pack Chrg flag lower down. The rest of the fields match the normal Quick Edit.
controls: Swiggy — list / unlist on Swiggy
Zomato — list / unlist on Zomato
Brand — which sub-brand catalogue the item belongs to
Swiggy Pack Chrg — apply Swiggy packaging charge
Save / Cancel
states.narration: On the aggregator menu, Quick Edit also controls the platform switches: Swiggy, Zomato, brand and packing charge.

states.title: Full Edit on an aggregator item — Platform Sync and Swiggy image
states.description: The aggregator Full Edit form has two extras. Under Item Image, a 'Swiggy Image' switch: 'Use same as Item Image' or 'Upload different image' (Swiggy has stricter photo rules). A 'Platform Sync' section holds the Swiggy, Zomato and Swiggy Packing Charge toggles and the Brand dropdown.
controls: Swiggy Image: Use same as Item Image — one photo for everything
Swiggy Image: Upload different image — separate uploader for Swiggy
Platform Sync: Swiggy / Zomato toggles — list on each platform
Platform Sync: Swiggy Packing Charge — apply Swiggy's packing fee
Platform Sync: Brand — sub-brand assignment
Save — writes item + both images in one multipart call
states.narration: Aggregator items can carry a dedicated Swiggy photo and their own platform switches — all in the Platform Sync section.

states.title: Aggregator Stock — Addon Stock tab
states.description: The Aggregator Stock button opens two tabs. Addon Stock lists every add-on used on the aggregator menu with Enable / Disable buttons per brand, and a catalog-level status that applies to all brands restaurant-wide (a warning explains this). Use it when an add-on ingredient runs out.
controls: Addon Stock / Variation Stock tabs
Brand dropdown — Main Brand or a sub-brand
Enable / Disable per add-on — stock ON / OFF on the aggregators
Catalog status warning — changes apply to ALL brands
states.narration: Out of one add-on, not the dish? Aggregator Stock lets you disable just that add-on across Swiggy and Zomato.

states.title: Aggregator Stock — Variation Stock tab
states.description: Variation Stock does the same for variation options (e.g. 'Large' size unavailable): each option can be enabled or disabled on the aggregators without touching the parent item.
controls: Variation Stock tab — switch from Addon Stock
Enable / Disable per option — stock ON / OFF
Brand dropdown — scope by sub-brand
states.narration: Same idea for variations: switch off a single size or portion on the aggregators while the dish stays live.

states.title: Status Configuration — station-level settings
states.description: Local Settings (Status Configuration) are stored per device / station, not per restaurant. This page controls how the order screen behaves on this terminal: order-taking mode, QSR mode, weight prompts, takeaway name / phone requirements, station view and — for menus — which menu this station actively sells from.
controls: Back — return to previous page
Enable all / Disable all — quick toggles for the visibility grid
Order-taking / QSR / Weight prompt toggles — order screen behaviour
Save — persists to this device; Reset — restores defaults
states.narration: Status Configuration is per terminal. It decides how this device takes orders — and which menu it sells.

states.title: Active Menu — which menu this station sells
states.description: The Active Menu block lists the restaurant's menus (Normal, Party, Premium…). The chosen one becomes the menu the order screen loads on this device: categories, items and prices all come from it. Default is Normal, so restaurants with one menu see no change. Save applies; the order screen picks it up on next open.
controls: Menu option buttons — Normal / Party / Premium (one active)
Save — stores the choice on this device
Reset — back to Normal
states.narration: Running a party in the banquet hall? Set that terminal's Active Menu to Party and it sells the party price list — other terminals are untouched.

states.title: Switching menus — Party menu selected
states.description: Selecting 'Party' from the menu-type dropdown reloads all categories and items with Party-specific prices. Party and Premium menus are priced independently from Normal.
controls: Menu type dropdown — select Party to view and edit Party-menu prices
Item counts — recalculated for Party menu
Item cards — show Party-menu prices and availability
states.narration: Need a separate party price list? Switch to Party here. Everything you see now belongs to the Party menu only — your Normal menu is untouched.

states.title: Full Edit — Allow Discount toggled ON (discount fields revealed)
states.description: When Allow Discount is switched on in Pricing & Tax, two new fields appear: Discount (a fixed rupee amount or a percentage) and Discount Type (Flat or Percent). The item can now receive a discount when added to an order.
controls: Allow Discount toggle — reveals Discount and Discount Type fields when ON
Discount — the amount or percentage value
Discount Type — Flat (fixed ₹ amount) or Percent (% of item price)
states.narration: Toggle Allow Discount ON and two fields appear — the amount and whether it is a flat rupee value or a percentage. Save to enable discounting on this item.

states.title: Food Variations — Multi-select group with Min and Max fields
states.description: Changing a variation group type from Single to Multi reveals two additional fields: Min (minimum picks required) and Max (maximum picks allowed). Use Multi for toppings, sides, or any choice where guests can pick more than one option.
controls: Single / Multi selector — switch to Multi to allow multiple picks
Min — minimum number of options the guest must select
Max — maximum number of options the guest can select
states.narration: Switch a variation group to Multi and Min and Max appear. Set the bounds — for example, pick at least 1, up to 3 toppings — and the cashier or guest is guided through the choice.

states.title: Quick Edit — complete form (all 12 fields)
states.description: Quick Edit shows all 12 frequently-changed fields on the card without opening the full form. The bottom half includes Tax Calc (Inclusive / Exclusive), Inventory and Packaged toggles.
controls: Name, Sold By (Unit), Category — identity fields
Price, Food Type, Complementary — core pricing and type
Tax Type, Tax %, Tax Calc — tax configuration
Inventory, Packaged — operational flags
Save (green) / Cancel — commit or discard
states.narration: Quick Edit puts the twelve most-changed fields right on the card. For anything deeper — variations, add-ons, availability windows — use the pencil to open the full form.

states.title: Add-ons master — inline edit row (pencil clicked)
states.description: Clicking the pencil on any add-on row in the master panel opens an inline edit form: name, price (in ₹), weight (in grams) and Veg / Non-Veg type. Save commits the change globally — the new price applies to every item the add-on is attached to.
controls: Name field — edit the add-on name
Price field — edit the price charged to guests
Weight (g) — optional, used when linked to inventory
Veg / Non-Veg — food type dropdown
Save — commits globally; Cancel — discards
states.narration: Click the pencil on any add-on to edit it in place. Change the price once here and it updates everywhere this add-on is used — no need to touch individual items.

pre_actions.js: (function(){ const rows = document.querySelectorAll('tr button, li button, [class*="addon"] button, [class*="row"] button'); if(rows.length > 0) rows[0].click(); })()

states.title: Bulk Editor — Validate Tax results
states.description: Clicking Validate Tax checks every item's tax configuration against the restaurant's registered tax slabs and highlights any items whose tax rate does not match a valid slab.
controls: Validate Tax button — triggers the slab check
Highlighted rows — items with mismatched or unusual tax rates
Tax Type / Tax % columns — the fields to correct
states.narration: Use Validate Tax after a bulk price revision or Excel import to catch any tax misconfiguration before it affects a guest bill. Correct highlighted items and validate again.

states.title: Bulk Editor — orange dirty cells (unsaved changes)
states.description: Any cell you edit in the Bulk Editor turns orange to signal an unsaved change. The footer shows how many dirty cells are pending. Reset All discards all changes; Save commits them all in one call.
controls: Orange cell — changed but not yet saved
Dirty cell count (footer) — number of pending changes
Save (footer) — commits all orange cells
Reset All (footer) — discards all changes and restores original values
states.narration: Orange means unsaved. Edit as many cells as you need — they all queue up. When you are ready, Save commits everything in one go. Not happy? Reset All undoes the entire session.

pre_actions.js: (function(){ const inputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('td input[type="number"], td input:not([type="checkbox"])')); if(inputs.length){ inputs[0].click(); inputs[0].select(); } })()

(function(){ const inputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('td input[type="number"], td input:not([type="checkbox"])')); if(inputs.length){ const inp = inputs[0]; const nativeInputValueSetter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window.HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set; nativeInputValueSetter.call(inp, String(Number(inp.value||0)+999)); inp.dispatchEvent(new Event('input',{bubbles:true})); inp.dispatchEvent(new Event('change',{bubbles:true})); inp.blur(); } })()

post_actions.js: (function(){ const btns = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button')); const rb = btns.find(b => b.textContent.trim() === 'Reset All'); if(rb) rb.click(); })()

states.title: Bulk Editor — category filter + select all items
states.description: After filtering by a specific category, clicking the header checkbox selects every visible item at once. The footer then shows the count and activates the Delete Selected button — enabling bulk deletion of an entire category's items.
controls: Category dropdown (filter strip) — narrows the grid to one category
Header checkbox — selects / deselects all visible rows at once
Delete Selected (footer) — removes all selected items (requires reason)
states.narration: Filter to a category, tick the header checkbox and every item in that category is selected instantly. Then Delete Selected to remove them all — the system will ask for a reason first.

pre_actions.js: (function(){ const sel = document.querySelector('[data-testid="bulk-editor-category-filter"], select[name="category"]'); if(sel){ sel.selectedIndex = 1; sel.dispatchEvent(new Event('change',{bubbles:true})); } })()

states.title: Quick Edit while Party menu is active — Party price visible
states.description: With the Party menu selected, Quick Edit on any item shows the Party-specific price. Changing and saving here updates the Party price without touching the Normal menu price.
controls: Price field — shows and edits the Party-menu price
Menu type context — changes here apply to Party menu only
Save — saves Party price; Normal price is unchanged
states.narration: While you are on the Party menu, Quick Edit shows the Party price. Edit it here and only the Party price changes — your Normal menu stays exactly as it is.

states.title: Aggregator Stock — Variation Stock with data
states.description: The Variation Stock tab lists every item that has variations, with each option (e.g. Small, Large) shown as a separate row. Each option can be enabled or disabled per aggregator platform independently.
controls: Variation Stock tab — shows all variation options across all aggregator items
Item name + variation option — each row is one selectable option
Enable / Disable per platform — control availability at the variation level
states.narration: The Variation Stock tab lets you disable a specific size or option on one platform without affecting others. For example, disable Large on Zomato while keeping it live on Swiggy.
